title: GEORGE CALLAGHAN BUILDINGS IN ...
reason: Pencil-signed G. Callaghan 83 lithograph titled Hamilton, 7/7 of a small edition; Callaghan is a Tasmanian-resident artist with a local following.
findings: Framed lithograph (grainy crayon lithograph texture) of a village street seen over corrugated iron roofs and brick chimneys, with stone cottages, a verandahed cottage, a Georgian two-storey building and gums. Pencil signature lower right in the margin reads 'G. Callaghan 83' (photo 2). Pencil title and edition lower left reads 'Hamilton 7/7' (photo 3) and a faint in-plate inscription at lower left appears to read 'Hamilton' too, so this is the last impression of an edition of 7, matching the catalogue wording. The scene most likely is Hamilton in the Tasmanian Derwent Valley (not confirmed). George Callaghan (born 1941 in Northern Ireland, settled in Tasmania about 1973, painter and graphic designer, per web biographies) is a Tasmanian-linked artist and the 1983 date fits, but the signature has not been matched to his hand. Reference only: a Callaghan lithograph 'Nocturne' Ed. 6/22 carried a A$150-200 estimate at Colville Auctions, Hobart, 6 Aug 2024 (estimate only, seen 19/10/2026 at https://www.invaluable.com/artist/callaghan-george-nnbh4yf89l/sold-at-auction-prices/). Small edition and local subject suggest better than a typical decorative print (my estimate A$150-350).
condition: Print looks sound with no tears seen and lightly toned edges; the cream mat has brown foxing and water-stain spots; plain timber frame, appears glazed; not examined out of the frame.
rescore_note: Pencil-signed G. Callaghan 83 lithograph 'Hamilton' 7/7 fits the Tasmania-based George Callaghan, but he is a modest-value artist: his lithograph Nocturne 6/22 carried a $150 to 200 estimate at Colville, Hobart, 6 Aug 2024 (invaluable.com, seen 19/10/2026); foxed mat and signature not matched to his hand; my estimate $100 to 200.
